chapters.html:
Mydei has experienced over a thousand deaths.

Rather ironic considering he was called Mydeimos the Undying. His first experience with life was dying as a child. And then it was a cycle of dying and drowning and living for nine winters because learning to swim whilst drowning as soon as you come back to life was arguably a little hard. This was all to say pain wasn't something that bothered him.

Medically speaking, drowning was supposed to be one of the most painful ways to die according to that journal Hyacine had given him. (“You don't value your life enough, Lord Mydei, so I can only hope to appeal to you by giving you this book.” She had told him once after treating his injuries despite him telling her not to bother.) Since he's drowned to death more than a thousand times it only made sense that he didn't flinch even in the face of decapitation.

Phainon was rather upset when it had happened, his hand making aborted moves towards his neck for the rest of that month. He didn’t understand the sentimentality but he let it slide. He looked like he was about to cry, after all.

So it truly took him by surprise when something as mundane as fingers brushing against his skin caused him to flinch and for his breath to hitch.

Like all things out of norm in his life—minus the usual stuff—it was because of Phainon.

His hand had brushed against the bare skin of his waist as he had walked past him, the touch accidental from how narrow the passage had become with the afternoon crowd in the Marmoreal market.

A foreign noise had escaped Mydei’s lips, choked and breathy. It was out even before he had a chance to bite his tongue, too surprised by the feel of the pads of Phainon’s sword roughened fingers against his bare skin. The place he had touched tingled, the touch making him shiver with a feeling he's never felt before.

This unfortunately did not escape Phainon’s notice. The man despite his playful teasing was meticulous when it came to studying people. It was unnerving at first but Mydei had gotten used to it. He didn’t really appreciate it at the moment, though.

He stepped closer, his head cocking to the side like an overgrown puppy. His blue eyed gaze dropped down to his waist for a moment before looking back up at him.

“...Are you hurt, Mydei?”

“...No. I was just startled.” Mydei muttered, looking away as he felt a surge of mortification. Thousands of deaths he had conquered and he flinched from a simple touch?

A surprised gasp escaped his lips when a palm cupped his waist. He looked up at Phainon, shivering when he saw how intently Phainon was studying him, his blue eyes stripping him bare.

The combination of his calloused palm cradling Mydei’s bare waist and those intense blue eyes studying him made him feel unusually hot, his head lightheaded. The skin under Phainon’s palm tingled deliciously, making him bite his lip to stop any incriminating sound from coming out. He pressed his palms against Phainon’s firm chest, his cheeks burning with embarrassment and his lungs feeling two sizes smaller.

“Just what. Do you think you are doing.” He bit out with a snarl, the clawed tips of his gauntlet digging into Phainon’s chest. No one has ever dared to touch him so brazenly, no one has ever thought to touch him outside of violence. The feeling was so foreign, the warmth and roughness of Phainon’s palm against his skin made his head spin, his teeth digging harder into his lower lip as he felt something like a whine make its way up his throat when Phainon’s fingers gently pressed into his flesh. Phainon studied his face, a small smile pulling at his lips. His warm blue eyes curved into mischievous crescents.

“Are you, perhaps…ticklish?”

Mydei growled, finally pushing the man away with a huff. He crossed his arms defensively, choosing to glare at Phainon’s well endowed chest instead of his face. The belt that ran across his chest to fasten his pauldron and cape always looked like it worked overtime keeping his chest from spilling out of his shirt.

“Do you usually go around groping people and asking if they were ticklish? Is that a pastime of yours, Deliverer?” He bit out, the place where Phainon’s hand had been still scalding hot.

“G-groping…?” Phainon stammered with wide eyes, his cheeks pink.

“I simply placed my hand on your waist!”

He squawked indignantly, unfortunately attracting the attention of the street vendors and citizens.

“Besides you didn't answer my question!” Phainon said with a pout, opening his stupid mouth again to probably mention how Mydei was brought to his knees from just a simple touch when everyone was watching them and Mydei—

Mydei simply turned around and walked away. He did not run, no. He walked briskly with wide steps. He was not running away, he was strategically retreating.

When he made it back to his sleeping quarters and put his teleslate on silent mode he hoped Phainon would drop this subject and never bring it up again.

***

He knew it was wishful thinking to ever hope that Phainon would ever forget anything. The Deliverer of the Flame Chase was unfortunately a tenacious man.

He had remembered Mydei’s preference for sweets, noticed he liked chimeras, knew the measurements of his body, his calculation of the circumference of his waist and his bust size more accurate than what he even remembered. So it was to no one’s surprise that Mydei was put to the test as soon as he was woken up.

“You know…you could have been a little softer with the punch.” Phainon grumbled as he leaned back in the bath, looking very unbothered by his purpling cheek despite his complaints.

“And you could have woken me up like you always do by shaking my shoulders instead of blowing a raspberry into my belly.” Mydei growled, crossing his arms. His ears were still burning from the encounter, the spot where Phainon’s lips and tongue touched was still tingling with a weird warmth. Phainon whined, his lips comically turned upside down as he waded to where Mydei was lounging, a little farther than he usually did after Phainon’s stunt.

“I just want to know if you’re ticklish!” Phainon asked, his hand coming up to play with Mydei’s braid like he couldn’t stand still without messing with him. Mydei made an irritated noise in his throat, ignoring the weird feeling in his chest as Phainon gently played with his braid.

“...And what will you do with information like that?” He asked, resigned and weary. It was already alarming to him that he couldn’t even handle touches that were considered casual between friends, too used to rough clasps on his shoulders and slaps on his back and much too familiar with blades lodged into his chest and fists against his skin. Gentle touches like absently touching his waist with sword worn fingers or blowing raspberries into his skin was so alien. Phainon cocked his head, looking too much like a clueless chimera, raising the hand holding the braid to brush the back of his knuckles against Mydei’s cheek.

“I want to learn everything about you, even the endearing sides…especially the endearing ones.” He said with a smile that displayed his dimples, his face stupidly handsome and his demeanour too stupidly charming. He sighed, already feeling himself giving in, mortification burning his skin as he looked away, his arms tightening in their crossed position against his chest.

“I…” He began, the shame making him a little nauseous as he squeezed his eyes shut.

“I’m not used to touches that aren’t ones that happen on a battlefield.” He said, his voice soft. The silence that followed was uncomfortable so much so that he wanted to leave and maybe go outside and kill black tide creatures and titankin instead, maybe go on a week-long expedition and return and hope Phainon would just forget everything. When he turned around to go and do just that, a firm hand wrapped around his wrist. His breath hitched, his cheeks heating as he gently attempted to tug his hand from Phainon’s grip.

“...Let go.” He said, quiet and ashamed.

He gasped when he was pulled into a warm body instead, his breath stuttering in his chest when he felt sturdy arms wrap around his waist and pull him into a gentle embrace, his back bumping into Phainon’s bare chest. He felt soft hair against his cheek and a nose against his neck.

“...What are you doing?” He asked, unable to control the tremor in his voice. Everything was so warm and smelt like Phainon, like bulrushes and sunwarmed clothes and it was all a little too much. He wanted more. His hands remained frozen by his sides, his eyes wide as he stared sightlessly in front of him.

“I’m sorry for teasing you in the market…I didn’t know.”

Phainon said, genuinely sounding contrite. Mydei felt a hysterical chuckle escape him, the absurdity of the situation a bit much for him.

“Why are you sorry about this? There was no way you could have known, Deliverer.”

Mydei gasped when Phainon wrapped his arms tighter around him, his eyelashes now tickling the skin of his neck from the proximity.

“I…want to introduce you to…non violent touches if that is okay.” Phainon murmured into his skin, making Mydei’s skin burn, his head dizzy with overstimulation, his chest sweetly aching with a foreign emotion.

“...You are a fool.” He managed to say, hoping his voice sounded calm and even. At this point, Phainon had him fully in his embrace, his generous chest pressed against his sensitive back, his lower half a respectful distance away. It was nice, too nice. The warmth engulfed him, melting his brain and making him hyper-aware of the gentle strength of Phainon’s embrace, his warm scent, his soft hair, his really…really nice voice—

“If…that is the case…can you start smaller?” Mydei said, his voice embarrassingly cracking, knowing full well that he was probably red from head to toe now. He hopes Phainon thinks it's the bath or at least doesn’t acknowledge it. His pride can’t take anymore beatings today. He heard Phainon make a noise of surprise, his arms loosening their embrace and his warmth retreating. Mydei still felt the ghost of it against his skin, he wished to feel that warmth again and it scared him.

He turns back to see a sheepish Phainon, relieved to see his cheeks were pink with embarrassment too.

“H-how about I wash your hair?” Phainon asked, fidgeting nervously when Mydei didn’t immediately answer.

“I-I won’t touch anything else I swear.” He said in a rush, his blue eyes watery and earnest, again, a little too reminiscent of a chimera. Mydei sighed, still unsure of the arrangement but unable to entirely deny Phainon when he was being this earnest.

“Be quick. I will allow it only if it is for about one-eighth a quint” he said, turning away and closing his eyes, his shoulders stiffening when he felt Phainon wade close to him again. He was led by his shoulders to be close to the lip of the bath beside the toiletry, swallowing when he felt light touches on his hair, too faint to be properly felt.

“I’ve always thought your hair was rather voluminous and soft for someone who regularly drenches himself in ichor.” Phainon murmured almost absently before he felt fingers card through his hair and brush his scalp, the tension in his shoulders melting before he even registered that it did, sagging a little against the man behind him with a sigh.

“Good?” he heard Phainon ask, the smile in his voice blatantly obvious.

“You haven’t even started washing my hair, Deliverer. Don’t be so smug.” Mydei grumbled.

Phainon huffed a helpless laugh, the click of a bottle and the squeeze of product heard before he started lathering the shampoo into Mydei’s hair. A soft noise escaped his throat when Phainon massaged his scalp, his eyelids fluttering and threatening to close from how good it felt. His fingers were thorough and firm in a way that was so unfamiliar, too used to people taking advantage of his long mane to yank it in battle. He bit his lips when he realized he just wouldn’t stop making soft helpless noises, the gentle pressure on his scalp addicting.

He didn’t realize he had slumped even more against Phainon to the point that his back was against his chest again, his shoulder blade tingling from the reverberation of Phainon’s soft laugh.

“I can’t wash your hair like this! You’re like an overgrown chimera.” Phainon said with a louder laugh, his chest shaking with it and it all felt so…so good. Too good for someone like him, someone so used to violence.

“Between the two of us, you resemble a chimera more with your huge, protruding eyes.” He grumbled and stood straighter, smiling when he heard Phainon squawk.

“Pro…Protuding?!” He said indignantly, grabbing the bucket beside him and upturning a deluge of warm bathwater over Mydei’s head with no warning. Mydei growled, turning around, grabbing Phainon by the shoulders and pushing him into the water.

“Wait! Wait, I need to—blurblelble—put conditioner in your hair!”

***

Phainon was surprisingly gentlemanly about learning about Mydei’s weakness. But that also meant he was a little awkward.

“You…ah…um. Can I braid your hair?” Phainon asked a few days after the incident at the bath. Despite learning about Mydei’s sensitivity to touch he didn’t push him during any of the baths that followed the hair washing. His hands twitched and he looked like he wanted to ask Mydei every single time but he stopped himself at the last minute, opting to simply talk Mydei’s ear off like he usually did. He didn’t mind that either. Contrary to what most people believed, he truly enjoyed Phainon’s company.

It was nice to have the companionship of a man with strength that rivaled his, with a personality as sweet as his and charm so magnetic he pulled Mydei into his orbit without realizing it. When he was with Phainon he could simply be Mydei and not Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos.

It was also because of this that he lamented seeing him struggle so much, especially when the said struggle was because of him.

“Deliverer,” He said, looking up at the fidgeting man. They were seated in the Garden of Life with chimeras in their laps and Phainon had been eyeing his unravelled braid since they had entered. It had been at least two quints.

“You needn’t be so hesitant with me, I am not made of porcelain.” He said with a sigh, moving closer while being careful with the two chimeras sleeping in his lap and tilting his head, offering his unravelled braid to Phainon.

He felt trembling hands against his braid as if Mydei had offered him something precious.

“I didn’t want to overstep or make you uncomfortable…You seemed genuinely distressed after admitting what you admitted in the baths and I felt like I forced you to say it.”

He said quietly, his voice thick. His head was ducked down so Mydei couldn’t see his expression but he could see the slump of his shoulders.

“You…did put me on the spot.” He sighed when Phainon let go of his braid and meekly curled his hands back into his lap.

“...But that doesn’t mean I don’t appreciate anything you did.” He grumbled, feeling his face flush in embarrassment, unused to laying such tender feelings out in the open.

“...I enjoyed you washing my hair. I would like it if you did it again and if I could in turn return the favour and wash your hair.” He mumbled, looking away when Phainon’s head snapped up in surprise, his blue eyes sparkling and his cheeks pink and it was a little too much for Mydei. He shuffled closer with those glittering eyes and gently took hold of Mydei’s braid again, his large hands a little clumsy as they braided his hair.

The braid ended up being a little skewed and loose but Mydei kept it till the next day when it eventually unravelled.

After that, Phainon was a little bit more straightforward. Still a little unsure but pushing forward as was norm for him considering his bullheaded nature.

He held Mydei’s hand when they walked through the crowded agora, took to braiding Mydei’s hair as often as he could, his braids now more sturdy and neat. He even sat closer, his broad shoulder brushing Mydei’s bare one now when they squabbled or tangling his feet with Mydei’s under the table when they went out to eat. He even washed Mydei’s hair regularly, trying out different scented oils and shampoos every time. It felt almost indulgent, the days feeling too much like the melting of honeycakes in his mouth.

But alas, as most things do during an era of tragedy and strife, idyllic days of peace are only a temporary fleeting thing. They were called to cull a mass of black tide monsters that had cropped up in the dead city of Carmitis, Aglaea’s face severe in a way Mydei hadn’t seen in a long time.

“There is no one else we can spare. It will be only the two of you,” She said, looking pained by that despite her claims of being unfeeling and cold. Mydei simply put his gauntleted fist to his chest and grinned.

“The Deliverer and I have been cooped inside for far too long. You needn’t worry about rabble.”

Phainon seemed a little worried but that was not anything new. He simply bumped his shoulder against his and cocked his head towards the exit of the baths, jumping down from the heroes' baths to make his way to where Kokopo III was stationed.

“...She looked alarmed in a way I’ve never seen before.” Phainon said with furrowed brows, a little later into the journey. The both decided to take one Dromas, opting to not use the Century gate because of the possibility of another swarm of black tide creatures popping up when they were away. Their shoulders brushed and Mydei bit back the urge to move closer and press his entire arm against Phainon’s warm and firm one.

“It’s hard not to be. It’s been a while since we’ve seen this many in one of the fallen city-states.” He said with a sigh. While his words to Aglaea were confident it didn’t mean he wasn’t wary. He used to be a war general, he was not a fool.

“But we will simply clear the skirmish like we usually do. Stop fretting.”

He said with a grunt, smiling when he heard Phainon make an indignant noise, the tension in his shoulders having dissipated a little.

The clean up wasn’t going too bad.

The battlefield was the ruins of the city’s marketplace, a place that was once vibrant with life and known for its man-made lake—a water body used by many couples to cruise on canoes and to propose to loved ones. It was now stagnant and murky, even the eggs of waterborne insects and mucky algae that would usually inhabit abandoned water bodies gone without a trace.

The two of them worked really well on the battlefield. They could read each other’s moves and move on instinct, compensating for the other’s weak spots seamlessly. It was almost like a waltz, the intimacy of it always making Mydei giddy with a feeling he couldn’t name.

Maybe it was because he’d grown soft from all the pampering that he made a stupid mistake.

He’d been keeping an eye on Phainon in the periphery of his vision when he saw him fall, his heart seizing in his chest and his eyes widening in panic, missing a creature that came up to him in his brief moment of worry and cleaved his shoulder, causing him to stumble and lose footing, belatedly realizing just how close he was to the lake. The last thing he heard before falling into the depths of Carmitis’ once romantic water cruising destination was a muffled call of his name and then it was the rush of water and the muted pop of his eardrums as he began to sink into the depths.

His eyes widened, blind in the murky darkness of the water, his hands clawing upwards to the surface. It was like he was back in the sea of souls. The first thing his conscience had registered after being born was the agonizing burn of his lungs, too weak to cry out in pain as he died mere moments after being thrown into the waters. It was the only things he remembered for years, opening his eyes to the blinding black waters, the burn of his lungs, his soundless screams.

And here he was again.

He thought that would have been the last of it, trading his years of desolate loneliness and helplessness for the kinder pain of dying in the battlefield to blades. He desperately clawed his way to the surface, fighting his panic with the rationality of a seasoned war veteran. He could swim, he knew how to swim, he lived in the sea for years, this was nothing.

And yet his body was heavy, weighing him down, even as he tried to swim to the surface, his heart plummeting to his stomach when he realized that the creature who had attacked him was wrapped around him and struggling mindlessly, pulling the both of them under. Anxiety welled up in his throat, nauseating and cold, his breath hitching when he began to swallow mouthfuls of water after his lungs had given up on holding his breath, the familiar agonizing burn in his lungs unwelcome. He won't make it back up to the surface.

He kicked the creature pulling him down, ignoring the burning of his lungs and his hazy consciousness to dig his claws into corrupted flesh and rip and tear and rip more, his inevitable death making him more feral in his endeavor to at least kill one of these abominations before he died and began his futile attempts to reach the surface, his lips pulling back in a snarl as he felt death pull him closer in an embrace, ignoring the useless terror he felt in the pit of his stomach, tearing at flesh till he died.

His throat was thick with anxiety but he never forgot what he needed to do, what he needed to keep his people safe, to keep Phainon safe. So despite the cold clutches of fear he waded against the currents of death and clawed his way back to life.

He knew he'd be greeted by frigid water but it was nice to imagine being wrapped in Phainon's arms again like he did only once back in the baths. The embrace had been warm and the assuring weight against his back had been so good, the feeling of security so foreign that he didn't realize that's what it was until a few days later.

He missed that now, wished he got to embrace Phainon more, greedy for that scalding encompassing warmth.

He felt himself take a deep breath that rattled his lungs when his soul was forcefully pulled back into his body, immediately turning over to hack and cough up the stale water in his lungs, instinct raising his hackles when he felt something wrap around him right after and restricting the movement of his arms, the surprise of waking up trapped making him sink his teeth into whatever he could reach, his legs kicking out in alarm when the thing didn’t budge.

He didn’t understand, he was supposed to be in the bottom of the lake, did something pull him out and trap him? If yes, what happened to Phainon? By the titans…what happened to Phainon? He was so distracted because of a nonsensical mistake and his cowardliness and now Phainon—

“Mydei! Ghh—can you stop biting my shoulder?” He heard a familiar voice say, his senses slowly returning to realize the restriction around his body was just a gentle embrace, reminiscent of the one he and Phainon had shared in the heroes’ baths but this time he was on his back and Phainon was hunched over him. He released the pressure of his tightening jaws on Phainon’s shoulder and slumped back down, the fight or flight instinct in him fizzling away into nothing and being replaced by a bone-tired fatigue.

Phainon looked surprisingly fine with only smears of dirt on his cheek and clothes, the small cuts on his skin comparatively negligible to the nasty bite on his shoulder that was sluggishly bleeding and the deep scratch marks on his arms. It didn’t take him long to realize that those marks matched his gauntlets.

“You don’t need to worry about those,” He heard Phainon say gently, his eyes wildly snapping back to look up at him again.

His expression was soft, worried and pained, his hunched shoulders and his strong arms curled over and around him like he was protecting him, a bulwark in a raging sea. He didn’t try to struggle away from the embrace, his stomach twisting in guilt and something else, hating how Phainon’s expression simply turned softer after studying his face, unwrapping one of his arms from the embrace to cup Mydei’s cheek. It was all so achingly gentle and undeserving and his throat closed up, his eyes burning.

“...The enemies,” He managed to say around the lump in his throat, ignoring the tremble in his fingers as he snagged the cloth of Phainon’s overcoat.

“We made quick work of them, don’t worry your pretty little head.” He murmured with a teasing smile, the pads of his fingers brushing beneath one of Mydei’s eyes. His breath stuttered, a noise escaping him before he could stop it, his heart aching something fierce. This was all a little too much, the softness and warmth worse than a blade to his chest.

“I hurt you,” He said, his voice thick and rough, his throat feeling tender. Phainon simply huffed, curving his hand over the small of his back to scoop him up to a sitting position and making him lean against his chest, uncaring of the open wound on his shoulder.

“I startled you, you were in distress. I could have been a little more gentle whilst handling you but I didn't want you to remain in the water,” He said, cradling the back of his neck and making him put his whole weight against him. He wrapped him up in an embrace again, trapping Mydei’s hands against his chest.

“You have my thanks for saving me, I will make sure I return the favour in kind.” Mydei said softly, blindsided and lost.

“But I don’t understand why you—”

He began before pausing, unsure of how to express his confusion and ache.

“...When I used to have nightmares as a child, I used to rest better in the arms of my mother.” Phainon murmured against his hair, his hand absently stroking up and down Mydei’s spine, unaware of how close he was to Mydei’s weakness.

“After my village—After I left Aedes Elysiae, when nightmares plagued me I would remember the warmth of my mother’s embrace and despite it being something I will never feel again I used to take solace in what I could remember.” The pads of his fingers were rough but so…so gentle on Mydei’s bare skin. He shivered, unconsciously curling closer, embarrassment burning his ears. His hands balled into fists against Phainon’s bosom.

“I…was late to notice your fall, your absence, something I could only register when all the black tide monsters had fallen.” Phainon’s voice shook, his embrace tightening for a moment.

“When I realized what had happened, I dived down to save you and by the time I had taken you back out, you were cold.” He buried his face in Mydei’s neck, pulling him so close he was almost in his lap.

“You were pale and your eyes were wide and unseeing with terror and anguish, clawed marks around your throat.”

“Phainon,” He began, the ache in his heart almost as agonizing as the burn was in his lungs.

“When you woke up next you were making these…” He heard Phainon inhale sharply, his fingers trembling.

“These agonized noises in your throat and I couldn’t do anything until you regained lucidity and I thought that holding you close would—”

He heard him audibly swallow and take deep breaths as if he was trying to keep it together, the now noticeable shake in his hands against Mydei’s back giving him away. He gently separated him and shuffled backwards, his expression shadowed by the fall of his snow white hair as he ducked his head down, his hands clenched into fists and placed on his knees as if he was in repentance.

“I’m sorry…It was selfish. I wanted to be that comforting warmth for you after failing to have your back but I realize how overwhelming it would have been for—”

His breath hitched when Mydei simply closed the gap between them by crawling over and placing himself in Phainon’s lap.

“You are a fool.” He said simply, cupping Phainon’s cheeks to tilt his head and make their gazes meet again. Phainon looked surprised, his eyes red like he was going to cry. He sighed, making an awkward aborted movement to embrace the man he was sitting on before exhaling sharply and properly wrapping his arms around him. His anxious thoughts from before and the terror it came along with dissipated in the warmth of their embrace, a soft noise escaping him when Phainon returned the embrace after a moment.

“...It was nice. This—this is nice.” He murmured, hoping it was enough for Phainon to understand, too exhausted and hollowed out to say anything else, hoping he was able to convey his sincerity with just those words and his embrace.

He closed his eyes, a smile tugging at his lips with Phainon simply pulled him closer, the warmth making him feel like they were in their own world and not among the viscera of monsters in a city long fallen.

***

Something changed after that. Something that either of them refused to name.

The touches turned more casual and all encompassing, Phainon plopping beside Mydei on his bed and cuddling him after their late night baths, citing a clumsy reason of not being able to make it back to his quarters because he was tired. Mydei didn’t mind, indulging in the feel of firm muscles wrapping around him and warm breath against his nape. It was embarrassing to admit how secure he felt, the feeling so foreign to someone like him.

Mydei took to absently playing with the collar around Phainon’s neck and brushing his fingers over Phainon’s cheeks, secretly delighted by how pink they would turn when he did that without his gauntlets. So when Phainon embraced him from behind in the baths one day without a word, Mydei simply sank into the embrace, leaning his head into the crook of Phainon’s neck, his back brushing against the bare skin of Phainon’s chest.

It felt good, dizzyingly so. Phainon placed his hands in the divots of Mydei’s hips, hesitant at first before settling firmly there when he didn’t hear any complaining.
